text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The key opposition Socialist Party wants parliamentary elections in 1997 within the framework of a new constitution which would have to be agreed before then.
- A man held for four months in jail on suspicion of killing of the general director of prisons has been freed and is seeking compensation after others were subsequently charged with the crime.
- The paper has published documents which it claims proves allegations of misuse of authority by the leader of the Independent Trade Unions, Valer Xheka.

- Companies running pyramid schemes are posing a problem for the government. The International Monetary Fund wants the schemes shut down but the government is afraid of upsetting the large numbers of people who have invested in such schemes.
- Some companies running suspected pyramid schemes have said they were prepared to meet with a delegation of the International Monetary Fund but others have refused.
- The Albanian lek has stabilised at a strong level over the last four days.
- Germany's Preussag AG is expected to make the government a $100 million dollar offer to buy 80 percent of the Albanian chrome industry.
- The paper says the privatisation of strategic industries in Albania is expected to be chaotic.
- Albanian Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu has left for Austria accompanied by a large group of businessmen.
- The rightist European Youth is convening for three days in Albania.

- A firm, which announced three days ago that it would give a 100 percent return on money invested in it for two months, said the offer would be open till Thursday. Hundreds flocked to place their funds and waited for hours at the firm.
